title: Psalms Chapter 130 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 130 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 130 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 130.

questions.question: From where does the Psalmist cry unto the LORD in Psalms 130:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:1 states, 'Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 130:2, what does the Psalmist ask the LORD to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:2 says, 'Lord, hear my voice: let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.'

questions.question: What does the Psalmist request the LORD's ears to be attentive to in Psalms 130:2?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 130:3, if the LORD should mark iniquities, who shall stand?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:3 says, 'If thou, LORD, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?' implying no one can stand.

questions.question: In Psalms 130:1, who is the Psalmist crying out to?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 130:3 suggests that if the LORD kept record of sins, no one would be able to stand before Him.
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:3 says, 'If thou, LORD, shouldest mark iniquities... who shall stand?' indicating no one could stand.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 130:1 is described as a Song of degrees.
questions.explanation: The opening of Psalms 130:1 states, 'A Song of degrees.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 130:2 asks the LORD to ignore the voice of the Psalmist.
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:2 actually requests the LORD to hear the Psalmist's voice and be attentive.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 130:3 implies that some people could stand if the LORD marked iniquities.
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'If thou... shouldest mark iniquities... who shall stand?' implying no one could stand.

questions.question: In Psalms 130, which of the following comes first?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:1 begins with 'Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD,' which comes before the other actions.

questions.question: According to Psalms 130:2, what part of the LORD does the Psalmist ask to be attentive?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.'

questions.question: What is the Psalmist's action described in Psalms 130:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:1 states, 'Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD.'

questions.question: What is the Psalmist's attitude towards the LORD expressed in Psalms 130:2?
questions.explanation: The Psalmist requests, 'Lord, hear my voice: let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 130:3, who is addressed with the question 'who shall stand?'
questions.explanation: The verse reads, 'If thou, LORD, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?'

questions.question: In Psalms 130:2, what is the Psalmist's voice described as?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 130 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 130 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 130:4, what is found with the LORD that causes Him to be feared?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:4 states, 'But there is forgiveness with thee, that thou mayest be feared.' This shows that forgiveness from God is the reason He is to be feared, linking mercy with reverence.

questions.question: How does Psalms 130:5 teach us about the virtue of patience in faith?
options: By urging us to act quickly and decisively
By showing the psalmist waiting for the LORD and hoping in His word
By commanding us to forget past troubles
By instructing to rely on our own strength
questions.correctAnswer: By showing the psalmist waiting for the LORD and hoping in His word
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:5 says, 'I wait for the LORD, my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope,' emphasizing patient trust and hope grounded in God's promises, which is an example of faithful endurance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 130:6 compare the psalmist's waiting for the LORD to?
options: Those who watch for the morning
questions.correctAnswer: Those who watch for the morning
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:6 states, 'My soul waiteth for the Lord more than they that watch for the morning,' illustrating intense longing and expectation similar to those eagerly anticipating dawn.

questions.question: What is promised in Psalms 130:7 if Israel hopes in the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:7 encourages hope in the LORD, promising mercy and abundant redemption, teaching believers to trust God's compassion and saving power.

questions.question: How does Psalms 130:4-5 together teach about the relationship between forgiveness and hope?
options: Forgiveness leads to fear, which destroys hope
Forgiveness is unrelated to hope and waiting
Because of forgiveness with God, the psalmist waits and hopes in His word
Hope is based on human effort, not forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: Because of forgiveness with God, the psalmist waits and hopes in His word
questions.explanation: Verse 4 declares forgiveness with God, and verse 5 shows the psalmist waiting and hoping in God's word, linking forgiveness as the foundation for hopeful patience.

questions.question: What encouragement does Psalms 130:7 offer to those struggling with guilt or sin?
options: To hide their sins and avoid the LORD
To trust in the LORD for mercy and redemption
To rely on their own righteousness
To seek vengeance on their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: To trust in the LORD for mercy and redemption
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:7 calls Israel to hope in the LORD because He offers mercy and abundant redemption, encouraging believers to trust God despite their failings.

questions.question: A fellow believer feels overwhelmed by their sins and doubts God's forgiveness. Based on Psalms 130, what biblical truth should you remind them?
options: God marks iniquities but does not forgive
There is forgiveness with God, so they can hope and wait for Him
They must earn forgiveness through works
Forgiveness is impossible for great sins
questions.correctAnswer: There is forgiveness with God, so they can hope and wait for Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:3-5 explains that if God marked iniquities strictly, no one would stand, but because forgiveness is with Him, the believer can wait and hope in His word.

questions.question: What does Psalms 130:6 teach about the intensity of the believer's longing for the LORD?
options: The longing is casual and unfocused
It is less than those who watch for the morning
It is greater than the anticipation of those watching for dawn
It is indifferent to timing or circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: It is greater than the anticipation of those watching for dawn
questions.explanation: Verse 6 compares the psalmist's soul waiting for the LORD with those who watch for the morning, saying the soul waits more eagerly, showing deep desire for God's presence.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 130:5 teaches that the psalmist's hope is based on the LORD's word.
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:5 explicitly states, 'my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope,' showing the foundation of hope is God's word.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 130:3, if the LORD marked iniquities, many people would still stand righteous.
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:3 says, 'If thou, LORD, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?' implying that no one would stand righteous if God kept record of all sins.

questions.question: Why does the psalmist say they wait for the LORD in Psalms 130:5-6?
options: Because they hope in God's word and anticipate His salvation
Because they want to prove their patience
Because they are indifferent to God's timing
questions.correctAnswer: Because they hope in God's word and anticipate His salvation
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 show the psalmist waiting and hoping in God's word and waiting with intense longing, indicating trust in God's timing and promises.

questions.question: What practical lesson about prayer can be drawn from Psalms 130:2?
options: Prayers should be loud and public
God ignores the voice of supplications
We should pray earnestly, expecting God to hear attentively
questions.correctAnswer: We should pray earnestly, expecting God to hear attentively
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:2 says, 'Lord, hear my voice: let thine ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications,' teaching earnest prayer with faith that God listens.

questions.question: According to Psalms 130:8, what will the LORD do for Israel?
options: Leave Israel to their own devices
Redeem Israel from all his iniquities
questions.correctAnswer: Redeem Israel from all his iniquities
questions.explanation: Verse 8 promises that the LORD will redeem Israel from all iniquities, emphasizing God's mercy and forgiveness in action.

questions.question: How does Psalms 130:4-6 together instruct believers about combining reverence, patience, and hope?
options: By teaching that forgiveness from God inspires reverence, leading to patient waiting and hopeful expectation
By advising to avoid waiting and trust only in works
questions.correctAnswer: By teaching that forgiveness from God inspires reverence, leading to patient waiting and hopeful expectation
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows forgiveness causes reverence, and verses 5-6 show the psalmist patiently waits and hopes in God's word, linking reverence with patient hope.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 130:7 emphasizes that hope in the LORD is futile because He lacks mercy.
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:7 states, 'Let Israel hope in the LORD: for with the LORD there is mercy,' directly affirming that hope in God is well-founded due to His mercy.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 130 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 130.

questions.question: What does the psalmist urge Israel to do in Psalms 130:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:7 directly states, 'Let Israel hope in the LORD,' encouraging the people to place their trust and expectation in God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 130:8, what will the LORD do for Israel?
options: Redeem Israel from all his iniquities
questions.correctAnswer: Redeem Israel from all his iniquities
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:8 states, 'And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities,' showing God's forgiving and redeeming nature towards Israel.

questions.question: Which two qualities are attributed to the LORD in Psalms 130:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:7 says, 'for with the LORD there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption,' highlighting these key divine attributes.

questions.question: In Psalms 130:6, the psalmist compares his waiting for the LORD to what imagery?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:6 uses the metaphor of watchmen waiting for the morning to express eager anticipation for the LORD's coming.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently found in Psalms 130 through the repetition of 'wait' in verses 5 and 6?
questions.explanation: The repetition of waiting in verses 5 and 6 demonstrates parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device emphasizing the psalmist's patient hope (Psalms 130:5-6).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares the theme of redemption from iniquities as found in Psalms 130:8?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:25 states, 'I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions,' echoing the theme of God's redemption from sin as in Psalms 130:8.

questions.question: The Hebrew word often translated as 'redemption' in Psalms 130:7 is closely related to which concept?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'redemption' is linked to the concept of a kinsman-redeemer (goel), one who rescues or buys back, a significant cultural role in ancient Israel (Psalms 130:7).

questions.question: How does Psalms 130:4 describe the relationship between forgiveness and fear of the LORD?
options: Forgiveness encourages fear of the LORD
Forgiveness removes the need to fear the LORD
Fear of the LORD causes forgiveness
Forgiveness and fear of the LORD are unrelated
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiveness encourages fear of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:4 states, 'there is forgiveness with thee, that thou mayest be feared,' meaning that God's forgiveness inspires reverence and awe.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of redemption from sin found in Psalms 130:7-8?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:7 speaks about redemption through Christ's blood, paralleling the theme of plenteous redemption from sin in Psalms 130:7-8.

questions.question: What is the primary emotional tone conveyed by the psalmist in Psalms 130:1-2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:1-2 depict a cry 'out of the depths' and a plea for God’s attentive hearing, expressing deep desperation and humility.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 130:3, if God were to mark iniquities, no one would be able to stand justified before Him.
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:3 says, 'If thou, LORD, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?' indicating that no one could stand if God held sin against them.

questions.question: The phrase 'A Song of degrees' at the beginning of Psalms 130 refers to what characteristic?
questions.explanation: In Hebrew tradition, 'Song of degrees' indicates a song sung by pilgrims ascending the steps to the temple, fitting the theme of spiritual ascent in Psalms 130:1.

questions.question: Which theme in Psalms 130 is foreshadowed by the concept of 'plenteous redemption' in verse 7?
questions.explanation: The abundant redemption mentioned in Psalms 130:7 foreshadows the Messiah’s redemptive work, a key theme developed in the New Testament.

questions.question: Which verse directly emphasizes the psalmist's reliance on God's word as a source of hope?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:5 states, 'and in his word do I hope,' showing the psalmist’s trust in God’s promises as a basis for hope.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 130 portrays the LORD as both merciful and just, emphasizing only mercy without justice.
questions.explanation: While Psalms 130 highlights mercy (130:7), it also acknowledges God’s justice implicitly, as seen in the fear inspired by forgiveness (130:4). It does not emphasize mercy without justice.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 130 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 130 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 130:1 indicate about the psalmist's condition?
options: He is in a state of joy
He is crying from the depths
questions.correctAnswer: He is crying from the depths
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:1 states, 'Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD,' indicating a deep emotional or spiritual distress.

questions.question: According to Psalms 130:4, what is available with the Lord?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:4 says, 'But there is forgiveness with thee,' emphasizing God's merciful nature.

questions.question: What does the psalmist express about waiting for the Lord in Psalms 130:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:5 notes, 'I wait for the LORD, my soul doth wait,' indicating a deep, patient expectation.

questions.question: In Psalms 130:7, what is the psalmist encouraging Israel to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:7 states, 'Let Israel hope in the LORD,' calling for trust in God's mercy.

questions.question: What does Psalms 130:3 imply about human righteousness?
options: No one can stand before God
Only the righteous can approach God
questions.correctAnswer: No one can stand before God
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:3 poses the question, 'If thou, LORD, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?' indicating human inability to stand before God's holiness.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 130:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:7 mentions, 'for with the LORD there is mercy,' showcasing God's merciful character.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'more than they that watch for the morning' signify in Psalms 130:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:6 emphasizes the psalmist's intense hope and longing for the Lord, comparing it to the anticipation of morning.

questions.question: According to Psalms 130:8, what will the Lord do for Israel?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:8 states, 'And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities,' affirming God's promise of redemption.

questions.question: What does the psalmist mean by 'thine ears be attentive' in Psalms 130:2?
options: God listens to the righteous only
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:2 implores, 'Lord, hear my voice: let thine ears be attentive,' indicating the belief that God hears and listens to supplications.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God does not forgive sins. What does Psalms 130:4 teach?
options: There is forgiveness with the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: There is forgiveness with the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:4 clearly states, 'But there is forgiveness with thee,' countering the claim that God does not forgive sins.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 130:5 and 6 convey about hope?
options: Hope is only for the righteous
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:5-6 conveys that true hope in the Lord is characterized by patient waiting and deep longing.

questions.question: What doctrine is reflected in Psalms 130:8 regarding redemption?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:8 teaches about God's redemptive work, promising to redeem Israel from all their iniquities.

questions.question: How does Psalms 130 connect to the broader theme of hope in Scripture?
options: It reinforces the hope of redemption and mercy
questions.correctAnswer: It reinforces the hope of redemption and mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 130 emphasizes God's mercy and redemption, connecting to the overarching biblical narrative that highlights hope in God's saving grace.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is reflected in the phrase 'plenteous redemption' in Psalms 130:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:7 speaks of God's 'plenteous redemption,' highlighting His grace in providing abundant forgiveness.

questions.question: What does the psalmist's cry from the depths illustrate about human experience in relation to God?
options: Humans call out to God in despair
questions.correctAnswer: Humans call out to God in despair
questions.explanation: Psalms 130:1 reflects the human experience of crying out to God in times of deep distress, seeking His help.
